identity: polyglot is a deliberately tiny test fixture, not a product: a 13-file, 255-line multi-language 'solution' committed inside the analyzer's own test suite. Its job is to exercise the analyzer engine across every supported tree-sitter language and the main component and relationship types, and to serve as the anchor for the P4-1 parity snapshot that the P4-7 cutover is diffed against. Every service in it (FastAPI api, TypeScript web client, Go worker, Rust/Ruby libs, Swift app, docker-compose db and cache) exists to trigger a specific detection path, not to do real work.
audience: Developers of the analyzer itself (and its test suite), inferred from the README since no other audience is documented. They open a map of this fixture to verify that the analyzer detected what the fixture was built to make detectable — languages, component types, entry points, the one declared relationship — and to diff parity snapshots when the engine changes. A reader treating this as a real system to operate or extend is misreading it.
what_matters: Coverage completeness: every language and component type the fixture was planted to exercise must appear in the map, because a missing one is an analyzer bug, not fixture noise
The single declared relationship (web client → api over HTTP) and its contract-backed boundary, since it is the only relationship signal the fixture provides
Entry-point detection correctness: api's port 8000 bind, worker's main.go, and the suspicious 'listens on a port' attribution on the markdown root
Stability of the map as a parity baseline: descriptions must be deterministic and grounded so P4-7 cutover diffs are meaningful
Not inflating: the map must present this as a fixture, since architecture verdicts (zone of uselessness, low activity) are artifacts of its purpose

criteria.statement: The map states explicitly that this is a test fixture for the analyzer, and every component description is framed as 'exists to exercise X' rather than as production functionality.
criteria.why: The fixture's only value is what it exercises; a map describing polyglot-api as a real API server would mislead the exact reader (an analyzer developer) checking detection behavior.
criteria.how_to_check: Read the identity/summary and each component description; any description that could apply to a real production service of that name fails.

criteria.statement: All eleven languages present in the tree (python, typescript, javascript, go, rust, ruby, swift, plus markdown/yaml/toml/json) are attributed to the correct component, with none silently dropped.
criteria.why: Language coverage is the fixture's reason to exist; a dropped language means the analyzer's tree-sitter path for it went unexercised.
criteria.how_to_check: Cross the languages histogram in the scale data against the language field of each mapped component; every code language must appear on exactly the component the README assigns it to.

criteria.statement: The web→api HTTP relationship is named with its direction and protocol, and the map notes it is the fixture's sole cross-component edge.
criteria.why: With total_relationships=1, this edge is 100% of the relationship-detection evidence; getting it wrong or omitting it invalidates the parity anchor.
criteria.how_to_check: Find the relationship in the map; it must run from services/web (or services/web/src) to services/api and say HTTP.

criteria.statement: The 'root' component's 'listens on a port' entry-point claim is either corrected or flagged as an attribution of docker-compose's db/cache port bindings, not left as-is.
criteria.why: A markdown/infrastructure root that 'listens on a port' will read as an analyzer bug to the fixture's audience; the map must resolve whether it is docker-compose signal bleeding upward.
criteria.how_to_check: Look at the root component's entry in the map and confirm the port claim is explained against docker-compose.yml rather than repeated verbatim.

criteria.statement: The 'zone of uselessness' finding on services/web/src is contextualized as expected for a fixture (nothing consumes the web client by design), not surfaced as an architectural defect.
criteria.why: Mechanical findings on a fixture measure the fixture's construction, not design failures; reporting it as a defect would tell an analyzer developer their tool misjudges fixtures.
criteria.how_to_check: Find where the map mentions services/web/src; the wording must attribute the unused flexibility to fixture design.

criteria.statement: Every enrichment target reached a terminal contract state.
criteria.why: An item still asking to climb is unfinished work, and a run that reports done over unfinished work is the failure mode the census exists to make visible.
criteria.how_to_check: The census has no items in the escalate state.

criteria.statement: Claims are grounded in evidence that checks out.
criteria.why: A claim without evidence you can point at is not an answer, and a form scorer cannot tell the difference.
criteria.how_to_check: The grounded fraction of the census, and the adjudicator's spot-check disagreement rate.

criteria.statement: What could not be established is visible as an honest gap, with a reason a reader can act on.
criteria.why: An honest map says what it does not know. A gap papered over with a plausible sentence is worse than a gap.
criteria.how_to_check: Every honest-gap item carries a non-empty reason.

weighting_adjustments: Shift effort from services/api (ranked #1 by fan-in) toward per-language completeness across the band-3/4/5 components; in a coverage fixture the tail components carry equal evidentiary weight to the head, and the mechanical ranking's importance bands do not reflect that.

Spend effort on the root/docker-compose infrastructure component: its 15 commits are the only git activity in the subject and its entry-point attribution looks wrong; it is where the mechanical signals most need adjudication.
Spend near-zero on deep symbol-level enrichment; 33 symbols across 255 lines means file-level description is sufficient, and per-symbol work would cost more than the whole fixture is worth.
idiom_warnings: Every component is deliberately minimal and mostly disconnected (7 of 8 have zero inbound dependencies, zero commits); this is fixture design, not dead code or abandonment. Do not escalate to explain 'why nothing uses libs/core' — the README's answer is 'to exercise Rust parsing'.

The README's instruction 'Keep it tiny. It is committed as real files and must parse fast in CI' is a hard constraint: apparent under-implementation (a 24-line Rust 'library', a 21-line Ruby 'package') is intentional.

The 'listens on a port' entry_point_because on the markdown root component is likely an analyzer attribution artifact from docker-compose.yml's db/cache services, not a property of any file at root; treat it as a signal to verify, not a fact to repeat.

Names like polyglot-api and polyglot-web mimic production naming conventions on purpose so the analyzer's framework detection (FastAPI, SwiftUI) has something real to find; the gap between the production-sounding name and the trivial body is the point.
